_comment: Corrections to the generated data for Ruth. Every entry needs why and source; the build refuses entries without them. Sources are BDB (checked on Sefaria's BDB, 2026-10-22, by content review B or the coordinator) unless stated. See docs/review/content-A.md and content-B.md.

H4843.why: Ruth uses the sense 'be bitter' (1:13) and Hiphil 'make bitter' (1:20), the Naomi/Mara wordplay; 'provoke' is another sense

H5162.why: Ruth 2:13 is Piel 'comfort'; TBESH's 'to be sorry: comfort' was cut to its first half

H1431.why: Ruth 1:13 is Qal 'grow up' (of sons); 'magnify' is Piel/Hiphil

H7704b.why: BDB: cultivated ground and territory (fields of Moab); 'land' collides with אֶרֶץ

H4772.why: BDB's sense; it also fits the singular written form in 3:14 without choosing between readings

H1350a.why: BDB: 'act as kinsman, do the part of next of kin', chiefly in Ruth

H1353.why: Ruth 4:6 is the right of redemption; the short definition shown was the root heading 'kin'

H3206.why: a newborn at 4:16; 'youth' collides with נַעַר

H3950.why: BDB: 'specifically glean, after the reapers' in Ruth 2

H3427.why: Ruth uses sitting and staying (2:14, 3:18, 4:1-4) as well as dwelling (1:4)

H7069.why: 'buy' alone takes a side at 4:5, 10 where the object is Ruth

H2428.why: BDB puts אֵשֶׁת חַיִל (3:11) under ability and worth; 2:1 and 4:11 differ

H2896a.why: 'pleasant' is narrower than Ruth's uses, including 'better' at 4:15

H1115.why: 'lest' collides with פֶּן; the short definition shown was the root heading 'failure'

H6485a.why: Ruth 1:6, the LORD visited his people

H7136a.why: Ruth 2:3, 'her chance happened on the field'

H4138.why: Ruth 2:11, the land of your kindred

H7997a.why: Ruth 2:16, pull out some for her; 'take' collides with לָקַח

H519.why: Ruth switches from שִׁפְחָה (2:13) to אָמָה (3:9); distinct glosses keep the switch visible without explaining it

H3212.why: BDB has one verb הָלַךְ; Strong's H3212 only splits off its יָלַךְ-type forms

H1980.why: one verb in BDB, including the forms Strong's lists as H3212

H2958.why: BDB treats the written form טְרוֹם (3:14) as a spelling of טֶרֶם

H227b.why: Ruth 2:7 מֵאָז הַבֹּקֶר, since the morning

H430.why: at 1:15 (Orpah's אֱלֹהֶיהָ) the number depends on the reader; 'God' alone takes a side

H5324.why: Ruth 2:5, 6, the servant set over the reapers; 'stand' collides with עָמַד

H2205.why: the elders of the town in Ruth 4

H5927.why: Ruth 4:1, Boaz went up to the gate

H1870.why: the capital in TBESH's 'Way' reads as a title

H3627.why: Ruth 2:9, the vessels the young men drew

H8252.why: Qal 'be quiet, undisturbed' (3:18 the man will not rest); 'to quiet' reads as causative

H7646.why: Qal 'be sated, satisfied' (2:14 she ate and was satisfied); 'to satisfy' reads as causative

H6642.why: BDB's only sense, 'reach, hold out' (2:14 he held out roasted grain); 'serve' is not in BDB

H4130.why: BDB 'kindred, kinship' (3:2 Boaz of our kindred); 'kinsman' collided with מוֹדַע at 2:1

H369.why: Ruth 4:4 denies existence: 'there is none besides you'

H4994.why: the short definition 'I' is a truncation of BDB's 'I pray'

H1961.why: the short definition 'fall out' is a sub-sense, not the meaning

H310a.why: the short definition 'the hinder' is the root heading

H5048.why: the short definition 'what is conspicuous' is the root heading

H5750.why: the short definition 'a going round' is the root heading

H6153.why: the short definition 'set' is the root heading

H834a.why: Ruth uses אֲשֶׁר of persons too (2:19, 2:20, 4:1, 4:14); the short definition 'who' is one use, not the meaning

H3588b.why: the two words form one phrase; TBESH's 'that if: except' was cut to 'that if'
H3588b.source: BDB p. 474 (closely conjoined כִּי אִם 'except'), confirmed by content review A

H518b.why: second half of the phrase כִּי אִם
H518b.source: BDB p. 474, confirmed by content review A

H996.why: the short definition 'interval' is the root heading, not the meaning of the preposition

H834c.why: Ruth 2:9 'from what the young men draw'

H673.why: Ruth 1:2 אֶפְרָתִים מִבֵּית לֶחֶם; 'Ephraimite' names the wrong tribe

H672.why: Ephrathah is Bethlehem in Ruth 4:11; the short definition shown was a run-on note

H8009.why: spelled שַׂלְמָה in 4:20 and שַׂלְמוֹן in 4:21; the same English name hid that

H7706.why: the meaning of the name is debated; 'Almighty' is the traditional rendering

H3068.why: TBESH's 'title' class covers months and gods; this is the divine name

H3063.why: the land of Judah in 1:1, 2, 7; the man Judah in 4:12

H3478.why: Israel in Ruth is the people (2:12, 4:7, 11, 14)

_stems._comment: A verb's sense in a stem other than Qal, used for the English of each form. Stem codes are OSHB's (N Niphal, p Piel, P Pual, h Hiphil, H Hophal, t Hithpael, v Hishtaphel, l Pilpel). Checked against BDB under each stem.

H7604.why: Niphal 'be left, remain' (1:3, 5 she was left)

H5702.why: Niphal 'be shut in, i.e. shut oneself off' (only here)

H4843.why: Hiphil 'make bitter' (1:20 Shaddai made me bitter); the Qal 'be bitter' is 1:13

H7999a.why: Piel 'repay, recompense' (2:12 may the LORD repay your work); 'complete' is the Qal sense

H3498.why: Hiphil 'leave over' (2:14, 18 what she had left over); 'remain' is the Niphal

H3637.why: Hiphil 'put to shame, humiliate' (2:15); the gloss 'be humiliated' is the Niphal

H3318.why: Hiphil 'bring out' (2:18 she brought out what she had left)

H3045.why: Niphal 'be made known, make oneself known' (3:3, 14); Pual participle 'known one' (2:1 written form)

H3943.why: Niphal 'twist oneself, turn over' (3:8, only here)

H3190.why: Hiphil 'do well, make good' (3:10 you made your kindness better)

H3772.why: Niphal passive (4:10 the name will not be cut off)

H7673a.h: to cause to cease, leave without
H7673a.why: Hiphil 'cause to cease, let be lacking' (4:14 has not left you without a redeemer)

H1949.why: Niphal 'be in a stir', of a city (1:19)

H4772.why: a plural of רֶגֶל 'foot'; the written form at 3:14 is singular, the read form plural, so each gets its own English

H430.why: a plural form used both for God and for gods; 1:15-16 is left open, as in the gloss

H2205.why: the plural is used as a noun, 'the elders' of the town (4:2, 4, 9, 11)

H7934.why: 4:17 the women neighbors (plural); BDB's 'inhabitant, neighbour' keeps it apart from רֵעַ 'neighbor'

_participles._comment: Verbs whose participle is used as a noun in Ruth: the English is the noun, with 'the', 'our', 'of' as the form has them.

H1350a.why: the participle גֹּאֵל is the noun 'redeemer, kinsman' (2:20, 3:9, 12, 4:1, 3, 6, 8, 14)

H4191.why: the participle מֵת is 'dead' (1:8, 2:20, 4:5, 10); 'dying' misreads it

H413.note: Not אֵל 'God' (with tsere; not in Ruth) and not אַל 'not' (with patach). אֶל 'to, toward' has segol and is usually joined to the next word by maqqef: אֶל־.
H413.why: the same consonants as two common words; easy to misread

H408.note: Not אֶל 'to, toward' (segol). אַל 'not' (patach) negates a wish or command: אַל־תִּקְרֶאנָה 'do not call' (1:20).

H376.note: Not אֵשׁ 'fire' (tsere, no yod; very common).
H376.why: proposed in docs/review/renderings-1.md section 3; meanings and pages checked in BDB

H802.note: Not אִשֶּׁה 'offering made by fire' (segol; common in Leviticus).
H802.why: proposed in docs/review/renderings-1.md section 3; meanings and pages checked in BDB

H3899.note: Same letters as the verb לָחַם 'fight' (mostly Niphal נִלְחַם; common).

H7121.note: A second root קָרָא means 'encounter, befall', as in לִקְרַאת 'to meet'. Compare קָרָה 'happen' (2:3).
H7121.why: proposed in docs/review/renderings-1.md section 3; meanings and pages checked in BDB

_renderings._comment: Per-word corrections to the generated English, each with a reason and a source.

08Uv6.why: Niphal jussive used impersonally: 'let it not be known that the woman came'

08CGY.why: לְפָנִים as an adverb of time, 'formerly', not 'to the face'

08jGA.why: Hiphil participle in construct with נֶפֶשׁ: 'a restorer of life'

084W9.en: you (f pl) will shut yourselves off
084W9.why: Niphal reflexive, inflected for the addressees

083iR.why: the suffix is the object of נָגַע: 'not to touch you'

084Ed.why: pausal form (athnach) said to Boaz, so 2nd masculine; the data's 2fs tag is shown as OSHB has it

08sHf.why: impersonal: 'it is very bitter to me'

08GmF.why: impersonal Hophal: 'it has been fully told to me'

08F88.why: the subject is מִקְרֶהָ 'her chance', not a person

08TW6.why: the subject is יַד יְהוָה; 'she' would read as Naomi

08H3W.why: impersonal: 'that it may be well for you'

08pu1.why: the subject is the child, 'he shall be to you a restorer'

08vdQ.why: 'may the one who noticed you be blessed'

08NQN.why: נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה 'take as wife'; 'lifted' misleads here

08ssA.why: לְ 'as, for' with the participle used as a noun

08Ap3.why: 'be or become old': I am too old to be with a man

08WeU.why: a known crux: the data tags אֵת as the object marker after מִן; left literal, no reading chosen

08ygU.why: the written form is a participle of יָדַע used as a noun
